claims.text: Existing techniques for hallucination detection rely on intricate fuzzy, specific free-language-based chain of thought (CoT) techniques.
Parameter-based hallucination detection methods suffer from interpretability issues.
Methods that identify hallucinations post-generation cannot prevent their occurrence.
Post-generation hallucination detection methods suffer from inconsistent performance due to the influence of the instruction format.
Post-generation hallucination detection methods suffer from inconsistent performance due to the influence of model style.
SELF-FAMILIARITY evaluates the model's familiarity with the concepts present in the input instruction.
SELF-FAMILIARITY withholds the generation of responses in the case of unfamiliar concepts.
SELF-FAMILIARITY reduces hallucinations by emulating the human ability to refrain from responding to unfamiliar topics.
SELF-FAMILIARITY demonstrates consistently superior performance compared to existing techniques across four different large language models.

evidence.description: The authors validate SELF-FAMILIARITY across four different large language models, demonstrating consistently superior performance compared to existing techniques.

methodologies.name: SELF-FAMILIARITY
methodologies.description: A pre-detection self-evaluation technique that evaluates model familiarity with input concepts and withholds responses for unfamiliar ones.

limitations.text: Existing techniques rely on intricate fuzzy, specific free-language-based chain of thought (CoT) techniques.
Parameter-based methods suffer from interpretability issues.
Methods that identify hallucinations post-generation could not prevent their occurrence.
Post-generation methods suffer from inconsistent performance due to the influence of the instruction format and model style.
